text: Every Confidential-PII column needs a real control on who can see it, and leadership needs an ongoing way to check the whole program is holding up. This lesson builds both.
Anyone can request access with a business reason. It routes to the domain's named business owner for approval. And it expires in 90 days -- nothing stays granted forever by default.

Purview enforces this natively only for our Azure SQL source. Everywhere else -- Salesforce, Oracle, Snowflake -- the approval is real and logged, but enforcement is a tracked manual grant in that system itself.

A weekly report tracks scan coverage, classification coverage, and glossary adoption, sourced straight from Purview's own insights and our existing export views -- so nobody has to just trust the program is working.
Access is controlled and the program is measured. Next: an auditor asks one sharp question that tests whether any of this actually holds.
